# Independent audit: physical normal Schur forms and owned-base costs

Sources read completely:

- `candidate 0e4cb84a76d46e82`
- `candidate a93878767eaeb0de`

Result: PASS with no mathematical repair required. The source verifier
`supporting computation verify_optimized_normal_schur_and_menu_curvature_two_sided.py` passes its
current 39 exact symbolic checks. The independent checker accompanying
this audit also compares actual rational polygon clipping with the stated
cap formulas; finite checks supplement the classical all-parameter proofs.

## 1. Positive-definite and singular normal optimization

The C2 hypothesis is stated for a stable proper/transverse chamber, not
deduced from mere properness. The implicit-function argument with positive
normal Hessian K produces one local stationary minimum branch, and chain
differentiation gives A-B K^{-1}B^T with the stated sign and dimensions.
Globality is separately conditional on the compact gap to all other
normal directions; local stationarity alone is never used as a global
depth certificate.

For semidefinite K, orthogonal decomposition gives precisely the range
condition B^T v in range K. A nonzero null component allows arbitrarily
negative values of the linear-in-null-velocity quadratic model. When the
range condition holds, the pseudoinverse value and all minimizers are
correct. The example theta^4+h theta^2 correctly shows that this quadratic
calculation need not equal the reduced second derivative: the actual
response has order sqrt(|h|), and the reduced value is -h^2/4 on h<0.

For feasible equations Rw=d, completing the K-square gives the stated
pseudoinverse added cost. The residual e=d+R K^{-1}b lies in range R,
which equals range(R K^{-1}R^T); no independent-row assumption is missing.
With inequalities, the later note correctly retains the whole feasible
polyhedron instead of imposing all inequalities as equalities.

## 2. All-normal calibration and uniform compactness

At the centroid of the triangle of area 9/2, every ordinary own cap
has area at least 2. The complete proved triangle pairing identity
in `candidate 4ffd81a5b3e6f9fb`
puts the two endpoint contributions above 4 in every common direction
and at every tilt, including empty/full and supporting statuses.
Thus every nonvertical mixed cap has mass at least 6. Vertical caps
through the middle source capture two full fibers, of mass 9.

Equality in the ordinary centroid triangle inequality forces exactly
the three vertex-directed canonical caps: the one-vertex intercept
product has its unique minimum when the two intercepts are equal;
two-vertex caps have strictly larger area at the centroid. In one
canonical direction the opposite-threshold endpoint sum is 4+alpha^2
for |alpha|<=1. For |alpha|>=1 one endpoint is full, giving at least
9/2. Hence only alpha=0 attains endpoint sum 4. Cyclic vertex
permutation yields precisely the three displayed global minima.

The compact-gap persistence is justified, including moving bodies:
Section 1 of `candidate 867dbbe22c30cda2` preserves every
cap volume by replacing integer tilts with uniformly bounded tilts.
Its finite row family depends only on the unchanged finite bases.
All cap-support right sides stay uniformly bounded for the nearby
triangles and the fixed positive interior source. The same compact
normal parameter set therefore works throughout the family.
Cap masses are jointly continuous there: all continuous normals are
nonzero, their boundaries have zero fiber area, and the finitely many
nearby triangular fibers vary continuously. At the initial body the
complement of small neighborhoods of the three minima has a positive
gap. Uniform continuity preserves this gap for sufficiently small
parameters. Within each neighborhood, the positive normal Hessian
and implicit branch give the unique local minimizer. Thus the claimed
sufficiently small all-normal interval follows without an unproved
tilt-at-infinity exclusion.

## 3. Exact cap formula and actual compatible radius path

The one-vertex cap formula is obtained by dividing the retained vertex
margin by its two normal differences along edges. The differences are
3r_j and 3r_j(1-theta); multiplying the intercept product by
(9/2)r_j^2 gives the displayed mass exactly. This gives normal Hessian
diag(2,3), the stated mixed forces, and the physical reduced Hessian.
Its independent components agree with direct rational polygon clipping.

The path K_j=(1+a j)T is actual for |a|<1: the midpoint of its two
endpoint fibers is exactly T, and convex combinations in the total
convex hull have fiber radius 1+a z. Thus there are precisely the
three stated integer fibers and no hidden changed middle section.
The total mass is 27/2+9a^2. The exact local cap expression is

    6 + (3/2)theta^2/(1-theta)
      + (2a+alpha-a theta)^2/(1-theta).

Its minimizing local normal is (alpha,theta)=(-2a,0), with value 6
and positive Hessian determinant 6. The compact-gap argument above
turns this into actual source depth 6 for sufficiently small |a|.
The radius velocity has frozen cap curvature 8 and integer-tilt
Schur correction 8, so its optimized cap curvature is zero.

## 4. Exact whole-fiber coverage cost

For the three cyclic continuous normals, equal positive cover weights
balance exactly when all angular parameters equal a common theta.
The whole-space margin map over base j has image the plane whose
margin sum is j sum alpha_i. Thus coverage is equivalent to that
sum being nonnegative. Covering both endpoint fibers forces sum
alpha_i=0. This is explicitly whole continuous fiber-space coverage;
the note does not identify it with arbitrary coverage of just the
bounded actual body by one chosen group.

Under this equality the mean-square bound gives max_i Phi_i >=
6+4a^2, with equality at theta=alpha_i=0. This equals Gamma_2 M(a).
The freely optimized tilts have negative actual margins at the
centroid of the endpoint with a j>0, so their coverage defect really
occurs inside S on a positive-area neighborhood.

At second order variable positive cover weights do not change the
first integer-drift row, because all initial integer tilts vanish.
The tilt Hessian is 2I and its mixed force is (4A,4A,4A). Projecting
the free optimum (-2A,-2A,-2A) onto sum alpha_i'=0 adds 24A^2.
Zero angular velocities meet the other linearized balances, so
24A^2 is both necessary and attained. The stated multiplier 3/4
then gives 18A^2, the exact total mass second derivative.

## 5. Actual global maximum versus selected-group coverage

Every exposed endpoint has actual mixed depth equal to its ordinary
own depth: any selected continuous cap can be made to exclude all
other bounded fibers by a finite integer tilt. Thus its maximum is
2(1+a j)^2. For sufficiently small |a| these are strictly below 6.
The three optimized middle caps cover the entire middle fiber and
each has mass 6; their common actual source attains 6. Adding the
slack endpoint-isolating groups gives a complete cover, proving that
the actual global raw maximum is 6 while M(a) increases. This is a
local decrease of normalized maximum above the OC target, not an
OC counterexample or a universal extremal-body argument.

At a=1/2 the larger endpoint has exact depth 9/2. Cyclic triangle
symmetry and convex depth superlevel sets force the middle maximum
to occur at its centroid. A finite step tilt gives that centroid a
cap of mass 2+(9/2)(1/2)^2=25/8<9/2. This correctly certifies a
different globally deepest fiber without asserting the transition.

## 6. Shared-cap jets, ownership, and integrability

The exact first and second incidence equations retain each original
normal and threshold once, including the terms 2U_j.X_g. The cover
weight balance keeps its distinct derivatives and the terms
2mu_gj U_j. The projected drift acceleration correctly includes
nu a+2mu A+rho AA. A fixed integer source base adds no derivative.
An affine normal gauge has homogeneous second equations, whereas
a unit-normal gauge requires u.UU=-|U|^2 as stated.

At a tight ownership row a one-sided actual path requires first
coefficient nonnegative, and second coefficient nonnegative only
when the first vanishes. A two-sided path has first coefficient
zero. Rows with strict initial slack and identically zero source
rows are correctly separated. With first jets fixed the second
equations and required inequalities are finite linear constraints
on accelerations. They do not automatically integrate. The stated
full-row-rank implicit-function condition is a valid sufficient
condition for correcting an o(s^2) equality residual; strict first
or relevant second ownership slack then controls the finite rows.
Rows with both coefficients zero correctly remain unresolved by
jets alone.

## 7. Polyhedral Schur projection and finite stress

Only genuinely objective-absent variables can be projected into
auxiliary coordinates without cost. Positive-weight flat normal
modes with mixed body forces are explicitly not discarded. On the
stated positive-definite block, finite Fourier elimination makes
W(v) a closed convex polyhedron. The K-metric projection exists,
is unique in w, and realizes the exact square-completion formula.
Auxiliary realizers exist by the definition of the projection.

The equality/inequality multiplier signs are correct: gradients are
K(w-w0)+R^T lambda-G^T tau, with tau>=0, and the auxiliary stationarity
equation is S^T lambda-H^T tau=0. Polyhedral Farkas proves necessity
without a strict feasible point. Complementarity proves sufficiency.
Fixing active sets yields finite polyhedral parameter regions; the
unique optimizing w is linear on each, hence the value is piecewise
quadratic. This concerns the normal part for prescribed body velocity;
actual second budget claims still require the retained body/source
accelerations, individual cap inequalities, and integrability.

## 8. Exact two-group one-sided cost

The middle group assigned bases {-1,0} requires sum alpha_i<=0.
The right-endpoint group with integer coefficient 10 strictly isolates
its own fiber for all sufficiently small |a| and has mass 2(1+a)^2<6.
Its only ownership row is the identity zero. Its objective slack is
actual and no mass or original cap is omitted.

For a>=0 the free normal alpha_i=-2a is feasible and each mass is 6.
For a<0 put c=a(2-theta)<0. The mean alpha_i+c is <=c, so the mean
square is >=c^2. The exact same angular identity gives optimum
6+4a^2, attained at alpha_i=theta=0. Therefore the finite local-chamber
optimum is precisely 6+4(a_-)^2.

The corresponding projection cost is 24(A_-)^2 before the 3/4 stress,
and 18(A_-)^2 after it. The actual radius direction has volume curvature
18A^2 in both signs and is neutral separately on both parity classes.
The asymmetric ownership cost therefore cannot be a single quadratic
form determined just by parity. Reassigning which endpoint gets its
own slack group reverses the cost. This is an exact obstruction to
ignoring ownership, not a theorem selecting a valid ownership for all
hypothetical bad bodies.

`supporting computation verify_moving_normal_and_ownership_audit_slab_recovery.py`.
